spec.description: A 2015 apartment block in Nijmegen as its contractor planned it: the IFC model’s 3,505 elements drawn by Kepler Plus’s 4D Model layer on the day their tasks start and finish, played with the Time Brush, with the counts, the schedule and the S-curve in Mosaic following every frame, and the elements the as-built log has finished late.

options.content:
An apartment block of ten homes on the Schependomlaan in Nijmegen, built in 2015, as its contractor planned it: the architect's IFC model (3,505 elements) linked to the construction schedule, a 4D model. Brush the days or press play: the map shows the building at the brush's end, each element still to build as a faint outline, under construction in amber while its task runs, and built in the colour picked above, by kind of element or by the as-built log, which marks in red the elements whose task finished late. The counts, the schedule (amber as a task runs, grey once it is done) and the S-curve follow every frame, all in your browser. Tilt and turn the map with the right button or Ctrl+drag; hover an element for its task.

Data: [Dataset Schependomlaan](https://github.com/openBIMstandards/Archive-DataSetSchependomlaan) (TU Eindhoven, Hendriks Bouw en Ontwikkeling, ROOT, TNO, RAAMAC), CC BY 4.0: the as-planned IFC exported from Synchro, the planned and the as-built event logs (task names are the contractor's Dutch ones, in English beside them). The model stands on the building's outline in the Dutch building register (BAG); its colours are Pacha's, by kind of element. A planned schedule: the dates are the plan's, and the as-built log only says on time or late.

spec.rawSql:
-- Elements under construction each day, shell and structure apart from fit-out.
-- The brush's end is the instant the map, the counts, the schedule and the
-- S-curve show; it reaches the Mosaic panels through the build Selection.
SELECT time, active_shell AS "Shell and structure", active_fitout AS "Fit-out"
FROM $daily
ORDER BY time

-- The elements, coloured once built by the pick above (colour_by).
SELECT guid, task, task_nl, kind, ifc_class, as_built,
       CASE WHEN '${colour:raw}' = 'as_built' THEN as_built ELSE kind END AS colour_by,
       time, finish_date, latitude, longitude
FROM $parts

spec.query: Kind of element : kind, As-built log : as_built

query.rawSql:
-- One row per IFC element of the model (datasets/schependomlaan/build.sh): its
-- GlobalId names its part in model.glb, time and finish_date are its tasks' span
-- in the contractor's schedule. Every row carries the model's origin, which
-- places it: the centre of its plan, fitted to the building's outline in the
-- Dutch building register (BAG pand 0268100000084949).
SELECT guid, task, task_nl, kind, ifc_class, as_built,
       start_date::TIMESTAMP AS time, finish_date::TIMESTAMP AS finish_date,
       51.8418694 AS latitude, 5.8361778 AS longitude
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/schependomlaan/parts.parquet'

-- Each day of the build, where the elements stand at its start, as the map
-- draws them: started, built (their tasks finished), under construction (a task
-- running), still to build, built late (the as-built log), and the shares. The
-- brush keeps the days up to its end, so the largest count kept is the count at
-- the brush's end (and arg_max for the one that goes down again).
WITH p AS (SELECT *, start_date::TIMESTAMP AS s, finish_date::TIMESTAMP AS f FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/schependomlaan/parts.parquet'),
n AS (SELECT count(*) AS total FROM p)
SELECT d AS time,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s <= d) AS started_n,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE f < d) AS built_n,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s <= d AND f >= d) AS active_n,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s > d) AS still_n,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE f < d AND as_built = 'Finished late') AS late_n,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s <= d AND f >= d AND task <> 'Fit-out') AS active_shell,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s <= d AND f >= d AND task = 'Fit-out') AS active_fitout,
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE s <= d) / any_value(total) AS started_pct,
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE f < d) / any_value(total) AS built_pct
FROM generate_series(TIMESTAMP '2015-02-23', TIMESTAMP '2016-01-04', INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS g(d) CROSS JOIN n CROSS JOIN p
GROUP BY d
ORDER BY d

-- The contractor's tasks, each stamped (time) with its last day, so the brush
-- keeps the tasks that have finished by its end; finish_end closes the bar.
SELECT task, task_nl, start_date::TIMESTAMP AS start, finish_date::TIMESTAMP AS time,
       (finish_date + 1)::TIMESTAMP AS finish_end, elements, late,
       CASE WHEN late > 0 THEN late::VARCHAR ELSE '' END AS late_label
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/schependomlaan/tasks.parquet'

-- One row per task and day it runs: the brush keeps the days up to its end, and
-- the schedule fills each task's bar that far.
SELECT task, time, time + INTERVAL 1 DAY AS day_end
FROM (SELECT task, unnest(generate_series(start_date::TIMESTAMP, finish_date::TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL 1 DAY)) AS time
      FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/schependomlaan/tasks.parquet')
